meaning.evidence: All details kept: November 13, 2025 start, Recreation.gov and offices, the Walatowa Saturdays 9-4 from November 22 to December 20, 2024, pre-cut trees and priority, $10 non-refundable, $2.50 fee, 5 inch/10 foot tag rule, 15-foot example, Every Kid Outdoors, forest-health rationale.

sense.evidence: Terms fit: "Give us a bell for current opening hours", "get first dibs", "patches where heaps of skinny little trees are all crammed in", "where the wildlife can find a feed". "good for the bush" fits forest health in Aussie usage.

authenticity.evidence: Sounds like a friendly Aussie notice: "Good news if you're after a real Chrissie tree", "Just pop in the pass or voucher number", "heads up".

register.evidence: A level-2 touch: everyday Aussie words in a plain notice; no swearing.

tone.evidence: Stays an informative notice, though "Good news" and "here's a bonus" make it a bit more promotional than the neutral original.

flow.evidence: Reads smoothly, with the original's order intact.

variety.evidence: Varied: "Chrissie", "have a good read", "give us a bell", "first dibs", "pop in", "heads up", "the bush", "find a feed".

problems.why: Promotional framing added to a neutral notice.

problems.original: Cutting a Christmas tree also improves forest health

A.summary: A natural, complete level-2 notice with well-chosen everyday Aussie; slightly chirpier than the original.

meaning.evidence: Every fact kept, closely following the original.

authenticity.evidence: Plain, natural Australian English; nothing forced.

variety.evidence: Very few Aussie terms to vary; little to lean on but little there.
